title: How Agencies Can Measure Lead Response Time
metaDescription: A practical method for measuring your agency's lead response baseline and testing a 60-second service target without inventing industry benchmarks.
excerpt: Measure your own lead-response baseline, define eligible enquiries and test whether a 60-second service target is reliable and useful.

sections.intro:
Before changing a lead workflow, measure the one you have. Export form-submission and first-reply timestamps for a representative period, define which enquiries count, and calculate the median, upper range and no-reply rate.

This creates a baseline you can verify. It also prevents an industry average from being presented as though it describes your agency.

The useful question is whether a faster, more consistent first response improves your own process without reducing reply quality or hiding exceptions.
sections.fourCFit:
Lead response is a measurable Capability inside an AI Operating System. It depends on Connections to the form, inbox, calendar and CRM, plus Context for approved facts and voice. The Cadence layer handles any agreed follow-up after the first reply.

Because the event and timestamps are clear, this workflow can be compared against a real before-and-after baseline.
sections.whatDoneLooksLike:
A useful measurement plan records:

  • Eligibility: which enquiries should receive an automated first reply and which should be held for review.
  • Response time: form-submission timestamp to first-reply timestamp.
  • Coverage: eligible enquiries replied to, held, failed or missed.
  • Quality: factual accuracy, correct routing, appropriate tone and required human takeovers.
  • Commercial signals: qualification and booking rates observed before and after, without assuming causation.

sections.expectedResults:
The immediate result should be better measurement, not a promised conversion number.

  • You can see the real baseline and response-time distribution.
  • You can identify where delays, failures and handoffs occur.
  • You can test a service target against reply quality and team workload.
  • You can compare later commercial signals with the baseline while accounting for other changes.
sections.faq:
What if my lead volume is low?

Use a longer measurement window and review individual cases as well as summary statistics. A small sample should not be presented as a reliable conversion trend.

Does the prospect care if the first reply is automated?

That depends on the reply and the context. Test factual accuracy, tone, transparency requirements and the quality of the next step with your own prospects and team.

Can a human carry the service target?

Possibly. Compare staffing coverage, expected response time, workload and exception handling with the cost and risk of automation. The right mechanism depends on your volume and operating hours.
